what_its_for: Cromolyn is used to help prevent allergic reactions. Depending on the form you are using, it can help prevent allergy symptoms in your nose (like sneezing and runny nose), relieve itchy and watery eyes from allergies, prevent asthma attacks triggered by allergies or exercise, or treat a rare condition called mastocytosis that affects the stomach and intestines. It works by stopping your body from releasing the chemicals that cause allergic reactions. Important: this medicine PREVENTS symptoms — it does not stop an allergic reaction that has already started.
how_to_take: How you take cromolyn depends on the form your doctor prescribed: NASAL SPRAY — Blow your nose gently before using. Tilt your head slightly forward, insert the tip into one nostril, and spray while breathing in through your nose. Repeat in the other nostril. Avoid spraying into your eyes. EYE DROPS — Wash your hands first. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place the drops inside. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Remove contact lenses before use and wait at least 10 minutes before putting them back in. ORAL SOLUTION (for mastocytosis) — Open the ampule and mix the liquid into a half glass of hot water, then add cold water to cool it before drinking. Take it 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. INHALER (for asthma prevention) — Use exactly as your doctor instructs. Rinse your mouth with water after each use to prevent irritation.
dosing: Dosing depends on the form and your condition. Common dosing schedules are: NASAL SPRAY — Adults and children 2 years and older: 1 spray in each nostril 3 to 6 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. EYE DROPS — Adults and children 4 years and older: 1 to 2 drops in each affected eye 4 to 6 times a day. ORAL SOLUTION — Adults: 200 mg (2 ampules) four times a day, 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. Children 2 to 12 years: dose is based on body weight — your doctor will calculate the right amount. Children under 2 years: use only if directed by a doctor. INHALER — Follow your doctor's specific instructions. Always follow the exact dose your doctor or pharmacist tells you to use.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. Cromolyn works best when used regularly on a schedule, so try to take it at the same times each day.
storage: Store cromolyn at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not freeze any form of this medication. Keep the nasal spray and eye drops tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication past the expiration date printed on the label. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not use cromolyn nasal spray or eye drops to treat symptoms that have already started — it only works to PREVENT them, so use it before you are exposed to things that trigger your allergies. Do not wear soft contact lenses while using the eye drop form unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid touching the tip of the nasal spray or eye dropper to any surface, including your nose, eyes, or fingers, to prevent contamination. Do not stop using cromolyn suddenly without talking to your doctor, especially if you are using it for asthma prevention. If you use it for asthma, do NOT use cromolyn to treat a sudden asthma attack — always have a fast-acting rescue inhaler available.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience any of the following: severe stinging, burning, or irritation that does not go away after using the eye drops or nasal spray; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; your allergy or asthma symptoms are getting worse or are not improving after several weeks of regular use; you develop wheezing or shortness of breath after using the inhaled form; you experience chest tightness, nausea, headache, or joint pain that bothers you; nosebleeds that are frequent or severe with nasal spray use. Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately if you have a severe allergic reaction or a sudden, serious asthma attack.
when_it_works: Cromolyn does not work right away. It must be taken regularly for several days to weeks before you notice the full benefit. For allergy symptoms (nose or eyes), you may start to feel better within 1 to 2 weeks of regular use. For asthma prevention, it may take 4 to 6 weeks of consistent use before you get the most benefit. For mastocytosis (oral form), it may take 2 to 6 weeks to see improvement. Do not give up if it seems like it is not working right away — consistency is key. Always use it as scheduled, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: PREGNANCY — Talk to your doctor before using cromolyn if you are pregnant. It is generally considered one of the safer options for managing allergies during pregnancy, but your doctor should make this decision with you. BREASTFEEDING — It is not fully known how much cromolyn passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. CHILDREN — Nasal spray is approved for children 2 years and older. Eye drops are approved for children 4 years and older. Oral solution can be used in children 2 years and older with dosing based on weight. Use in infants under 2 years should only be done under close medical supervision. ELDERLY — No special dose adjustments are usually needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's instructions. KIDNEY OR LIVER DISEASE — If you have kidney or liver problems, let your doctor know, as dose adjustments may be needed, especially for the oral form.
